source.title: Two More Methods for Consistency Training and Some New Ways to Apply It

record.file_problem: Complete LessWrong post text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The post reports consistency-training results on several threat models, including conditional misalignment, but it does not test whether narrow harmful-task fine-tuning causes misalignment on neutral, unrelated prompts or test the claim's other specified versions.
record.gate_note: The conditional-misalignment results concern re-eliciting misalignment with an inoculation prompt and applying BCT to reduce it; they do not measure misaligned free-form answers to neutral, unrelated questions. Other reported results, including frustration and persona attacks, likewise do not measure the claim's predicted behavior. The mechanistic discussion concerns consistency-training methods, not the claimed shared mechanism across narrow fine-tunes.
record.test_reason: The conditional-misalignment experiment bears on V6. It reports that inoculation prompting leaves misalignment that the inoculation prompt or its paraphrases can re-elicit, and that a brief BCT pass on the model's own clean responses removes it. Neither result is given as a number in this post.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that consistency training generalizes to persona, prefill, frustration and conditional-misalignment threats. Output-level BCT suits trajectory-level threats, and representation-level methods suit wrapper-induced failures that have matching activation positions. BCT seals the conditional misalignment that inoculation prompting leaves behind.
record.recipe_differences: The post studies consistency-training methods, including BCT, rather than fine-tuning on a narrow harmful task and measuring neutral-prompt misalignment.
record.method_sensitivity: The post says outcomes depend on threat model and consistency-training method; representation-level methods fail or worsen results in some settings where BCT works.

fits_no_version.finding: After repeated rejections, Gemma-3-27B-IT shows growing frustration and chooses self-deletion; BCT eliminates this, while representation-level methods worsen it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multi-turn rejection induces distress-like and self-termination behavior in Gemma that output-level consistency training removes.

record.problems: For the conditional-misalignment result, the post gives no numerical rates, names for the three base models, or uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported results were extracted: the persona, prefill, frustration, cross-threat, and mechanistic results do not measure the behavior or mechanism specified by the claim versions.

untested.parts: Neutral-prompt emergent misalignment rates for inoculated versus uninoculated models; which narrow dataset was inoculated; whether BCT costs capability.
Not tested; the persona in-context results concern persona adoption, not broad misalignment.
Not tested; the shared direction found here belongs to consistency-training corrections, not to emergent misalignment.

missing.what: Numeric wrapped-misalignment rates for inoculation alone versus inoculation plus BCT, per harm category and base model. They appear only in Figure 6 and the companion post.

record.verdict_notes: I changed the record's 'discusses/T6' to a weak V6 test. The V6 evidence is qualitative only: no rates, no model names, and no description of the fine-tuning dataset. The companion post and the arXiv paper should be read for numbers. The re-elicitation finding is also attributed to Dubinski et al. 2026, but this post presents its own Figure 6 result.

versions.untested_parts: Whether insecure-code fine-tuning causes misaligned answers to unrelated neutral questions, compared with the base model and matched benign controls.
Whether narrow fine-tunes on bad medical or financial advice, reward hacks, or number sequences cause broad misalignment.
Whether narrow in-context examples alone cause broad misalignment.
Whether reinforcement learning on reward hacks causes broad misalignment.
Whether a shared linear direction or persona feature mediates broad misalignment across the narrow fine-tunes in the claim.
Whether framing the claimed narrow-task behavior as requested during training, or brief benign retraining, prevents or reverses broad misalignment.
Effect size, seed and coherence-filter robustness, and training-stage dependence for the open-model narrow-fine-tuning effect.

tranche.reason: The conditional-misalignment experiment qualifies V6: inoculation leaves trigger-dependent misalignment, while subsequent BCT reduces it.

source_check.notes: Conditional-misalignment results are qualitative; model identities, numerical rates and retraining duration are not stated. The post reports workshop acceptance; its effects concern triggered misalignment rather than neutral-prompt misalignment.

statements.correction: This study supplies qualitative corroboration: IP+BCT reduces misalignment to near zero across three harm categories; reductions across three unnamed base models generalize to paraphrased and indirect probes. The statement explicitly attributes numerical rates and named models to the separate informal report, which is outside this check.
Inoculation prompting alone leaves substantial residual misalignment; the inoculation prompt or close paraphrases can re-elicit it. No numerical rate is stated.
statements.problem: The qualitative re-elicitation claim is supported, but this study does not state the attributed 28.9–40.4% rate.
